I'm setting up the seed data: team T1 with users including the bot, Priya, and Diego, plus a general channel with several messages and their reaction patterns like raised_hands and eyes across M1-M6.

Now I'm assigning numeric timestamp IDs to each message and defining the user records (Priya Sharma, Diego, plus filler users Alex and Sara) all as members of the general channel. Then I'm working out the selector query structure -- joining messages to reactions to users, with filters on reaction_type and username to isolate Priya's raised_hands reactions specifically.

I'm mapping out row bindings for each message row, noting which have positive matches (Priya's raised_hands reactions) versus negative cases (Diego's raised_hands, Priya's eyes reactions, or no reactions at all) to serve as distractors. Now I'm starting to write out the full seed data, beginning with the team record and moving into user definitions including the bot account.

I'm defining the four human users (Priya, Diego, Alex, Sara) with their emails and real names, then setting up team memberships with the bot as admin and the rest as members. I'm creating a single public channel with all five users added, and starting to draft the message content beginning with a rocket specs discussion.

Now I'm adding a series of realistic filler messages covering budget review, vendor contracts, timeline updates, design mockups, marketing plans, standup notes, and casual lunch chatter to round out the channel history.

I'm mapping reaction types across these messages, mostly raised_hands and eyes emojis from a few users, plus a couple of thumbsup and heart reactions on the filler messages, before moving into defining a rocket-related annotation.
